changelog: - **Notification caps are counted per person, not per relation** (#2287). The dormant check-in budget and the weekly-report reminder were both capped on the `MentorshipRelation`, so a mentee holding two ACTIVE relations held two independent budgets — four "still interested?" mails where `docs/dormant-first-contacts.md` promises two, the second of which already says nobody will write again, and two identical report reminders every week forever. `sendDormantCheckIns` now decides on the person: the **sum** of `dormantNudgeCount` across their ACTIVE relations is the spend, and the **latest** `dormantNudgeSentAt` across them is the clock the 31-day spacing is measured from (the in-memory Set added in #2283 deduplicated one tick only, so the extra mail was deferred to the next run rather than cancelled). No column and no migration: both figures come from rows that already exist. `sendWeeklyReportReminders` collapses to one relation per mentee **before** the claim, picked deterministically by lowest id so two overlapping ticks race on the same `@@unique([relationId, weekStart])` row, and the new nullable `WeeklyReportReminder.recipientId` (plus `prisma/backfill-weekly-report-reminder-recipient.mjs`, wired into the deploy) makes "has this human been reminded this week?" answerable at all. The `@@unique([recipientId, weekStart])` that would make it structural is deliberately NOT in this change — deploys run `db push` before the backfills, so the index would be built against still-NULL rows and against exactly the duplicates at issue; it is the contract step, gated on the backfill's duplicate count reading zero on prod and shared preview, the same sequencing as #2286. Webhook and audit fan-out stay per relation, and the two mentor-facing sweeps (`checkMentorInteractionReminders`, `checkStageDeadlineReminders`) are documented as correctly per relation: their recipient is the mentor and each message is about a different mentee, so collapsing them would drop a deadline rather than a duplicate. With #419 holding, every number above is identical to today's — this is defence in depth, and a prerequisite if #1799 ever raises the per-mentee limit above one on purpose.
